protocol.name: treeland_snap_target_unstable_v1

protocol.description:
This protocol allows a client to request snap region hints from the compositor. While snapping is active, the compositor tracks the cursor position and notifies the client of the rectangle currently hovered by the cursor (e.g., a window boundary or a full output). The client uses these hints to draw its own snap preview UI.
Snap targets are computed against the window layout captured when the snap session starts: the compositor records the position and stacking order of every window at that moment and keeps them unchanged for the whole session. Windows that move, are mapped or unmapped, change stacking order, or are destroyed after start are not reflected in the snap targets.
A client may identify an overlay surface by setting the xdg-toplevel-tag "org.deepin.treeland.snap-mask" on that toplevel. When the compositor detects this tag, it applies the following configuration to the surface:
1. Raises the surface above normal windows and their popup panels. 2. Disables window open/close animations. 3. Excludes the surface from the multitask view and window switcher.
Such a surface does not affect the snapping protocol; snapping behaves the same whether or not the surface exists. Surfaces carrying the snap-mask tag are excluded from snapping, i.e., they are never reported as snap targets.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_snap_target_v1
interface.description:
This interface is a global singleton for requesting snap region hints from the compositor. Each client binds at most one instance of this global. The compositor tracks the cursor position and notifies the client of the rectangle currently hovered by the cursor.
The snap object is created in an idle state. The client starts snapping by calling start, which causes the compositor to capture the current window positions and stacking order and begin tracking the cursor position, providing snap region hints based on the captured layout.
While snapping is active, the compositor sends a snap_region event each time the snap target changes (i.e., when the cursor moves to a different window or output). A client that also needs to know which process owns a window snap target can enable the optional pidfd event by setting the event_type.pidfd bit in the events argument of start; without that bit the compositor sends no pidfd events. When enabled, and when the new snap target is a window with a determinable owning process, a pidfd event reporting that process is sent before the snap_region event it applies to. The client can use these events to update its snap preview UI.
When the client is done (e.g., the user has clicked or dragged to confirm a selection in the client's UI), the client calls stop to stop snap notifications. A stopped snap object may be restarted by calling start again.
Only one snap session may be active across all clients at any time. If another client's snap session is active, start fails with the snap_busy reason.

entry.name: snap_busy
entry.summary: another client has an active snap session

enum.name: event_type

description.summary: optional events a client can enable at start

enum.description: Bitfield of optional events the client may request when starting a snap session. Bits not listed here are reserved for future events and are ignored by the compositor.

entry.name: pidfd
entry.summary: report the pidfd of the process owning window snap targets

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_snap_target_v1 object. If snapping is in progress, the compositor automatically stops it (stops cursor tracking). No further events are emitted on this object.

request.name: start
request.description:
Request the compositor to capture the current window positions and stacking order and begin tracking the cursor, sending snap region hints based on the captured layout.
This request may be called again after stop to restart snapping; a fresh capture of the window layout is taken on every start. start must not be called on an already active snap object; the compositor ignores such a request.
The events argument selects which optional events the compositor may send for this session. It is a bitfield of event_type values: only the events whose bits are set are enabled, and passing 0 enables no optional events. Bits that do not correspond to a known event_type value are ignored. The selection applies to this session only; a start after stop establishes a new selection.
If snapping cannot be started because another client's snap session is already active, the compositor sends a failed event with the snap_busy reason instead.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: seat associated with this snap session

arg.name: events
arg.summary: optional events to enable for this session

request.name: stop
request.description:
Signal that the client is done with snapping. The compositor stops tracking the cursor and stops sending snap_region events.
This request is a no-op if snapping is not in progress (e.g., if failed was already emitted or stop was already called).
The client should call destroy afterwards to free the snap object.

event.name: pidfd

description.summary: pidfd of the process owning the snap target

event.description:
Reports the process owning the window that corresponds to the snap target reported by the next snap_region event. This event is sent only if the client enabled the event_type.pidfd bit in the events argument of start; otherwise it is never sent. When enabled, the compositor sends this event before the snap_region event it applies to, and only when the snap target is a window whose owning process can be determined. If the snap target is not a window (for example an output or empty desktop space), or the owning process cannot be determined, this event is omitted and snap_region is sent on its own.
No pidfd event is ever sent for a snap target whose window was destroyed after start: the captured region remains a snap target, but its owning process no longer exists.
The client owns the received file descriptor and is responsible for closing it. The descriptor stays valid independently of the snap session.

arg.name: pidfd
arg.summary: pidfd of the process owning the snap target

event.name: snap_region
event.description:
Notifies the client of the current snap target rectangle. The snap target set is captured at start and is fixed for the whole session: a window that moves, is mapped or unmapped, changes stacking order, or is destroyed after start does not add, remove, move, resize, or reorder the targets captured at start. In particular, a window destroyed after start keeps its captured region as a snap target. This event is sent each time the snap target changes due to cursor movement.
This event commits the snap target. A pidfd event, when sent for this target, precedes it and reports the process owning the target. When processing this event, the client should associate the most recent preceding pidfd event, if any, with this target; if no pidfd event precedes it, the target has no associated process.
The region is in global logical coordinates (i.e., the xdg_output logical coordinate space). The client is responsible for any coordinate transformation needed for its UI.
If width and height are both zero, there is no current snap target (e.g., the cursor is over empty desktop space). The client should hide its snap preview in this case.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: global logical x coordinate of the snap target

arg.name: y
arg.summary: global logical y coordinate of the snap target

arg.name: width
arg.summary: width of the snap target (0 if no target)

arg.name: height
arg.summary: height of the snap target (0 if no target)

event.name: failed
event.description: Snapping could not be started. The compositor will not send any more snap_region events. The client should call destroy to free the snap object.
